title: Signs an animal video is AI-generated

scenes.headline: Too cinematic to be wild
scenes.body: Movie lighting, perfect framing and a 'story' with a badger, all in a few seconds.

scenes.headline: Markings that drift
scenes.body: A real animal's stripes or spots stay the same from frame to frame. Watch for patterns that shift.

scenes.headline: No who, where or when
scenes.body: Real wildlife clips come with a filmmaker, a place and a date you can check.

scenes.headline: Look for the 'AI info' label
scenes.body: Meta asks creators to label realistic AI video and can add labels itself.

caption:
The owl is fake. The checklist is real.

Each tiger's stripe pattern is unique, which is why researchers can identify individuals from photos; generated animals often can't keep a pattern consistent.

Source: Meta newsroom (Feb & Apr 2024); Smithsonian's National Zoo. Real clip: Wikimedia Commons; AI clip: Google DeepMind Veo 3 demo (public domain), labelled on screen.
notes: AVOID format: anti-pattern explainer. The only AI footage is a public-domain Veo 3 demo, labelled AI on screen from the first frame and set against a real owl; we never publish AI animals as behaviour.
